title: Baseline and @scan:Suppress
description: The baseline is applied after suppressions and holds only unsuppressed findings. first() and second() hold the same line, so their findings share a hash: the suppressed one in first() is :1 and the baselined one in second() is :2. Removing first() renumbers it :1, and it stays baselined, since matching ignores the number. A suppressed finding is reported with baselineState new. Needs scan 0.15.0+.
upstream: BEP 1498: Finding fingerprints and baseline adoption (ballerina-spec/beps/tool-scan/1498_scan_baseline.md)

steps.name: --create-baseline
steps.note: 0 new issue(s), 2 in baseline, 1 suppressed. The file has 2 entries; the suppressed finding is not one of them.

steps.name: SARIF
steps.note: The suppressed result has baselineState new and a non-empty suppressions array; the other two are unchanged.

steps.name: --ignore-suppressions
steps.note: 1 new issue(s), 2 in baseline; exit 1. The count of the shared hash is now 2 against 1 entry, so the second in source order is new.

steps.name: first() removed
steps.note: The import is removed too, as nothing uses it.

steps.name: Scan after removing the suppressed one
steps.note: second() is renumbered from :2 to :1 and is still baselined: 0 new issue(s), 2 in baseline, no warning.

steps.note: Nothing is stale, but the kept entry is rewritten with its current value (:1): "Updated the fingerprints in the baseline at:".
